newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT ENDS 42 CENTS LOWER ON IRAQ, TECHNICALS.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT ENDS 42 CENTS LOWER ON IRAQ, TECHNICALS.

text.p: IPE Brent futures closed 42 cents lower on Friday after Iraq was given the green light by the United Nations to sell crude again for the first time since May, traders said.
Front month September settled at $18.48 a barrel after touching a low of $18.28. October finisbed 47 cents lower at $18.63.

Technical selling, weakening product prices in Europe and lower discussed values for physical North Sea crudes also helped lower the market in a roller-coaster session that saw numbers remain firmly in negative territory.
Some brokers said that a London opening under $18.50 a barrel on Monday would herald a rapid break below $18.00.
"I think $17.50 would be a reasonable target. That may sound aggressive but we have already seen some pretty sizeable moves today," one broker said.
The Brent front month had dipped to a fresh intra-day low of $18.56 after word that the U.N. Sanctions Committee had raised no objections to price formulas for the Iraqi exports.
The Iraqi crude is expected to start flowing next week under the second round of humanitarian oil sales.
Later news that U.S. oil company Coastal and trading firm Bayoil were expected to bring Iraqi crude to the Atlantic Basin helped propel values to a new low of $18.28.
Traders said some of the already had found buyers in the U.S. Gulf.
The underlying Brent cargo market was also weak despite good refining margins on both sides of the Atlantic.
Dated Brent was offered at around September -20 cents, the level Brent was traded on Thursday and some 38 cents lower than the previous reported deal. Bids were around -30 cents.
Oil products were also weak in Europe. A sharp drop in gasoline helped undermine Brent and gas oil barges were narrowly easier, although cargo differentials held firm.
Front month August gas oil settled at $169.50 a tonne, a dollar off the low, on good technical selling and weaker physical crude.
Chartists put support for August at $169.00 with initial resistance at $171, followed by a gap to $172.
Dealers said there was good demand for diesel into France but German demand was muted with many traders away from the office on holiday.
